value.name: Micky prepares for fight day
value.description: Micky dresses himself carefully and packs a suitcase, signaling that the day before the big fight has arrived.
evidence: Micky fixes himself in the mirror, straightening his button-down shirt, wears an ill-fitting sports coat, looks like a little boy playing dress up.
This is it, the day before the big fight.
value.location_hint: Micky's apartment above a two-car garage

value.name: Micky arrives at parents' house
value.description: Micky drives to his parents' house with his suitcase, where a limousine is already waiting outside.
evidence: Micky parks in front of his parents' house; a limo out front.
Micky opens the door, grabs his suitcase...

value.name: Alice and George prepare to travel
value.description: Alice and George get dressed up and pack for the trip, excited about the fight day.
evidence: Alice checks her hair, smooths her dress in the mirror.
George, dressed nicely, struggles to close their suitcase on the bed, whistling.
Both smiling, excited about the day, the fight.

value.name: Little Dicky is sent to Aunt Cathy
value.description: Alice tells Little Dicky to behave for Aunt Cathy so Dicky can help Micky win the fight.
evidence: LITTLE DICKY, 5, redhead, Dicky's son, runs in, followed by Pork.
ALICE (embraces Little Dicky) Little Dicky, listen to Mummy, you be good for ya Aunt Cathy so ya daddy can help ya Uncle Micky win a fight, OK?

value.name: Family gathers by limousine
value.description: Micky, Alice, George, and others stand around the limousine ready to leave, but Dicky is absent.
evidence: Micky, Alice, George, Pork, Sherry, and Red Rog standing around the limousine.
All dressed nice for their travel.

value.name: Mickey O'Keefe urges Micky to leave Dicky behind
value.description: Mickey O'Keefe says the family should go without Dicky and invokes a religious-sounding plea to let go.
evidence: MICKEY O'KEEFE (lowers his voice) It's none a my business, but I been goin' to meetin's, and they say let go and let Gahd.
You don't need this shit, Micky. Let's just go without 'im.
